title: 214. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Solving Exponential Equations Using Logarithms
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a basic exponential equation by taking logarithms of both sides.
questions.question: Solve \(2^x=10\).
questions.explanation: Take the logarithm base \(2\) of both sides of \(2^x=10\). This gives \(x=\log_2 10\). Equivalently, using natural logarithms, \(x=\frac{\ln 10}{\ln 2}\). The expression \(\log_{10}2\) is the reciprocal and does not satisfy the equation.
questions.hint: Apply a logarithm with the same base as the exponential expression.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation by using the change-of-base formula.
questions.question: Solve \(3^x=7\).
questions.explanation: Take natural logarithms of both sides: \(\ln(3^x)=\ln7\). Using the power rule for logarithms gives \(x\ln3=\ln7\). Therefore \(x=\frac{\ln7}{\ln3}\). The expression \(\frac{\ln3}{\ln7}\) is its reciprocal and is not correct.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation with a shifted exponent by isolating the exponential term and taking logarithms.
questions.question: Solve \(5^{x+1}=20\).
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by \(5\): \(5^x=4\). Then take the logarithm base \(5\) of both sides to obtain \(x=\log_5 4\). Equivalently, \(x=\frac{\ln4}{\ln5}\). The option \(x=\log_5 20\) ignores the factor of \(5\) already contained in \(5^{x+1}\).

questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation with a linear exponent by applying logarithms and solving for \(x\).
questions.question: Solve \(4^{2x-1}=11\).
questions.explanation: Take the logarithm base \(4\) of both sides: \(2x-1=\log_4 11\). Add \(1\) to both sides: \(2x=1+\log_4 11\). Divide by \(2\): \(x=\frac{1+\log_4 11}{2}\). The option without the added \(1\) does not correctly solve for \(x\).
questions.hint: After taking logarithms, solve the resulting linear equation for \(x\).

questions.learningObjective: Solve a natural exponential equation by taking the natural logarithm of both sides.
questions.question: Solve \(e^{3x}=5\).
questions.explanation: Take the natural logarithm of both sides: \(\ln(e^{3x})=\ln5\). Since \(\ln(e^{3x})=3x\), we get \(3x=\ln5\). Therefore \(x=\frac{\ln5}{3}\). The option \(3\ln5\) incorrectly multiplies instead of divides.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation with variables in both exponents by taking logarithms and collecting \(x\)-terms.
questions.question: Solve \(7^x=3^{x+1}\).
questions.explanation: Take natural logarithms of both sides: \(x\ln7=(x+1)\ln3\). Expand the right side: \(x\ln7=x\ln3+\ln3\). Bring the \(x\ln3\) term to the left: \(x(\ln7-\ln3)=\ln3\). Therefore \(x=\frac{\ln3}{\ln7-\ln3}\). The option using \(\ln7+\ln3\) does not follow from the correct algebraic rearrangement.
questions.hint: Take logarithms, expand, and collect all terms containing \(x\) on one side.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a more complex exponential equation by using logarithm laws and isolating \(x\).
questions.question: Solve \(2^{x+2}=3^{2x-1}\).
questions.explanation: Take natural logarithms: \((x+2)\ln2=(2x-1)\ln3\). Expand: \(x\ln2+2\ln2=2x\ln3-\ln3\). Move all \(x\)-terms to one side: \(2\ln2+\ln3=x(2\ln3-\ln2)\). Thus \(x=\frac{2\ln2+\ln3}{2\ln3-\ln2}\). Since \(2\ln2+\ln3=\ln12\) and \(2\ln3-\ln2=\ln\left(\frac{9}{2}\right)\), we get \(x=\frac{\ln12}{\ln\left(\frac{9}{2}\right)}\).
questions.hint: Take logarithms, expand both sides, and collect the \(x\)-terms together.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation by taking logarithms and applying logarithm laws.
questions.question: Solve \(5^x=2^{x+3}\).
questions.explanation: Take natural logarithms: \(x\ln5=(x+3)\ln2\). Expand: \(x\ln5=x\ln2+3\ln2\). Bring \(x\ln2\) to the left: \(x(\ln5-\ln2)=3\ln2\). Therefore \(x=\frac{3\ln2}{\ln5-\ln2}\). Since \(3\ln2=\ln8\) and \(\ln5-\ln2=\ln\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)\), the solution is \(x=\frac{\ln8}{\ln\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)}\).

questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation with coefficients in the exponents by using logarithms.
questions.question: Solve \(3^{2x+1}=4^x\).
questions.explanation: Take natural logarithms: \((2x+1)\ln3=x\ln4\). Expand: \(2x\ln3+\ln3=x\ln4\). Move the \(x\)-terms: \(\ln3=x(\ln4-2\ln3)\). Thus \(x=\frac{\ln3}{\ln4-2\ln3}\). Since \(\ln4-2\ln3=\ln\left(\frac{4}{9}\right)\), the solution is \(x=\frac{\ln3}{\ln\left(\frac{4}{9}\right)}\). The option with \(\ln\left(\frac{9}{4}\right)\) has the wrong sign in the denominator.
questions.hint: After taking logarithms, collect all \(x\)-terms on one side and factor out \(x\).

questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation with variables in both exponents and a shifted exponent.
questions.question: Solve \(2^x=5^{x-1}\).
questions.explanation: Take natural logarithms: \(x\ln2=(x-1)\ln5\). Expand: \(x\ln2=x\ln5-\ln5\). Bring the \(x\)-terms together: \(\ln5=x(\ln5-\ln2)\). Therefore \(x=\frac{\ln5}{\ln5-\ln2}\). Since \(\ln5-\ln2=\ln\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)\), the solution is \(x=\frac{\ln5}{\ln\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)}\). The option with \(\ln\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)\) has the wrong sign in the denominator.
questions.hint: Take logarithms, expand the right side, and collect all \(x\)-terms on one side.
